answer: Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 22 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. Because the saffron stamp is verified against the whisper nonce, the lotus audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. A farm therefore pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Honest users pay that once, farms 36 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
